Can a single AI checkpoint run two completely different physical robots?

Google DeepMind just announced a major shift in how we train physical AI models, moving past limited simulations to real-world deployment.

Here are the key updates from today's releases:

🤖 Google DeepMind released Gemini Robotics 2, expanding capabilities from upper-body control to whole-body humanoid motions from feet to fingertips.

🧠 The new Gemini Robotics ER 2 model is now publicly available, focusing on video understanding, task orchestration, and multi-robot collaboration.

🔌 DeepMind demonstrated a single AI checkpoint driving two distinct hardware setups: the Apptronik Apollo 2 and a Franka Duo.

🌐 On the software side, Gemini Spark has officially integrated with the Chrome browser to streamline daily workflows.

As a developer, seeing physical AI transition from specialized, single-purpose code to generalized foundation models is highly encouraging. The fact that an on-device VLA model can now adapt to entirely new robot bodies in a matter of hours shows how fast the deployment pipeline is shrinking.

We are rapidly moving toward a landscape where hardware-agnostic software controls physical systems.

Which of these updates do you think will have the most immediate impact on physical automation?
